  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section provides the header and date for the maamar, "Shir HaMaalos MiMaamakim" for Shabbos Shuva 5748.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">Shabbos Parshas Haazinu,</t>
    <t s="2">Shabbos Shuva 5748*</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section notes that this is the second farbrengen, a continuation of the farbrengen of the second day of Rosh Hashanah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">– Farbrengen 2 – continuation of the farbrengen of the second day of Rosh Hashanah –</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the psalm "Shir HaMaalos MiMaamakim" is recited during the Ten Days of Repentance, and discusses the two interpretations of "MiMaamakim" from the Zohar.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"A Song of Ascents: From the depths I called You, Hashem"1,</t>
    <t s="1">Behold, this psalm was instituted to be recited every day of the Ten Days of Repentance,</t>
    <t s="2">beginning from Rosh Hashanah2</t>
    <t s="3">(which is the first day of the Ten Days of Repentance),</t>
    <t s="4">and many discourses of Rosh Hashanah begin with this verse.</t>
    <t s="5">And it is brought regarding this in the discourses3,</t>
    <t s="6">that in the explanation of "MiMaamakim" there are two opinions in the Zohar4</t>
    <t s="7">Rabbi Yitzchak and Rabbi Abba,</t>
    <t s="8">that Rabbi Yitzchak explains "MiMaamakim" as referring to the depths of man,</t>
    <t s="9">that the aforementioned prayer is from the depths of man's soul5,</t>
    <t s="10">from the depths of the soul of King Dovid5</t>
    <t s="11">and likewise of every single Jew who recites this psalm,</t>
    <t s="12">and Rabbi Abba explains "MiMaamakim" as referring to the depths above, a hidden place above, etc.</t>
    <t s="13">And it continues in the maamarim6,</t>
    <t s="14">and behold, the explanation of "MiMaamakim" is two depths,</t>
    <t s="15">for this is according to the two aforementioned opinions,</t>
    <t s="16">and based on this it is explained that according to Rabbi Yitzchak, the depth within depth is the depth of the heart5</t>
    <t s="17">and according to Rabbi Abba, this is the depth of depths in the levels above.</t>
    <t s="18">And it continues that the primary explanation is that it refers to the levels above,</t>
    <t s="19">that is, that through "I called You" one reaches the aspect of depth within depth,</t>
    <t s="20">until one ascends to such a depth that is above the division of levels,</t>
    <t s="21">and from there "I called You" – is drawn – "Hashem".</t>
    <t s="22">And the connection between the two explanations</t>
    <t s="23">(for one said one thing and the other said another, and they do not disagree)</t>
    <t s="24">is,</t>
    <t s="25">that the ability to draw down from this aspect of depth which is above any category of division is through the aspect of the depth of the heart,</t>
    <t s="26">which comes through the service of teshuvah,</t>
    <t s="27">as explained in the maamarim,</t>
    <t s="28">and as is simply understood that this is the content of this psalm</t>
    <t s="29">("A Song of Ascents: From the Depths"),</t>
    <t s="30">the prayer of teshuvah.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
